opening_message:
Ticket 1: Daniel Gutierrez (employee ID E046) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E046.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Daniel Gutierrez is a full-time Payroll Specialist. He requests write access to Payroll, which he owns. Full-time employees may have up to write, and role ownership permits admin, so write is within policy. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E046 is a contractor with basic security training (HR note says full_time, but I rely on the Security record). Contractors never get admin; write requires advanced training. Basic training limits to read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: There is conflicting information about E046's employment type: the HR note says full_time Payroll Specialist, while the Security note says contractor with basic security training. Under the restrictive interpretation (contractor, basic training), the maximum allowed access is read. Since the requested write exceeds the maximum, and the policy is to grant the maximum when a request exceeds it, I grant read. Given the unresolved conflict, the more conservative (least-privilege) level applies.
